compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

physical.material: Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories

configs.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships 32620-703, doors fitted, without accessories.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.
each door opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so it is drawn as one fitted plate and the side it swings from is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover

gaps.note: no held page dimensions a guide: the arm, the head and the width are read by eye from the photographs and the page 2 figure.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side view of one guide

gaps.note: the data sheet says the guides align with rack units and gives no count; 48 a side on each face is the nominal 84 in over one rack unit.
gaps.wanted: the number of rack units the manager spans

gaps.note: the matrix prints the width (6 in) and the height (7 ft) as sizes to order by; only the depth is printed as an overall figure, so the width and the height are drawn at their nominal values.
gaps.wanted: an overall width and height, or a dimensioned drawing

gaps.note: only the overall depth is printed; the two channels and the centre section are each drawn a third of it less the doors (198), read from the proportions of the page 2 figure, which is not to a stated scale.
the data sheet and the installation drawing show an integral central track and no held page gives its width or how far it stands; it is drawn as a strip the full depth between the doors.

the manager ships with four accessory rods, rotating fingers, cable bundle swivels and half spools (the data sheet, page 1; no fingers or spools on the 6 in and 8 in widths), which fit anywhere on the track; none has a fixed place, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of a manager as shipped, with the accessories placed

gaps.note: the data sheet (page 6) sells a Mid Panel Kit that covers and divides the front and rear of the double-sided manager; it is not part of the manager as shipped, so the centre is drawn open.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the manager as shipped

gaps.note: the front door has a logo plate at the top and both doors have two blue latches on the back (installation instructions, page 3), the figure on that page shows a hook on the inside of the front door, and the data sheet's page 1 photograph shows a lighter vertical strip down the front door; no held page gives their size or position, so the logo plate, the blue latches and the inside hook are not drawn and the two doors are the same plain plate.
each door is drawn as a flat plate 3 mm thick at the end of its channel; no held page gives its section.

the manager attaches to the rack with carriage bolts; how far it stands from the upright, where the rack's rails fall in the centre section and the rearward bias on a 3 in rack (installation instructions, page 2) are never dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to a rack

gaps.note: the matrix says only Black; the shade drawn is read from the maker's renders of the fitted part, which no page gives as a colour value.

gaps.wanted: `attrs.physical.weight-kg` (profile `passive` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - material, finish and the indoor-only statement are the specifications table (page 1): 'Steel and aluminum with plastic T-shaped cable guides and plastic accessories', 'Black or Glacier White powder coat paint'. The matrix (page 3) gives the colour of this part and its black fingers.

bottom.note: estimated - the bottom end is the top end again.

chassis.note: estimated - 150 mm wide, 2133.6 mm (7 ft, 84 in) high and 600 mm deep. THE DEPTH IS THE DATA SHEET'S (matrix note, page 3: 'Overall depth for Double-Sided manager is 23.6"D (600 mm)'); THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL (matrix, page 3: 6" (150) and 7' (2.1)), taken here as the overall size, which the matrix does not say they are. The section is therefore estimated as a whole, and the figure of each dimension is in the entry that uses it.

color.note: estimated - 'Black' (matrix, page 3); the shade is the near-black of the data sheet's photographs of the fitted part, which are renders. The guides are black on every part number of this style.

door.note: estimated - the data sheet (page 1) lists a dual-hinged front door and a rear door assembly, pre-installed, and the installation instructions (page 3) draw the rear door as one plate; that the doors exist is printed, but no page prints a size of a door, so each is drawn as one plate of the manager's nominal width and height (the door components carry the method). A door opens to the right or to the left and lifts off; the format has no hinge, so the side is a gap. The front door has a logo and the rear door is plain; neither logo is drawn.

fingers.note: estimated - A GUIDE TO EACH RACK UNIT, 48 A SIDE ON EACH FACE, 192 IN ALL. The data sheet (page 1) says the side assemblies carry T-shaped cable guides 'that align with rack-mount unit (U) spaces on rack'; no page counts them. 48 is the nominal 84 in over 1.75 in, a column from the foot to the top of the manager. A guide is an arm 12 high with a head 30 high and 20 wide, read by eye from the page 1 photographs and taken to be the same on every width and on both faces.

front.note: estimated - the front channel with its door fitted. With the door off the front is the channel between the two side assemblies, the heads of the guides down each edge and the central track between them. The channel is 110 wide, the nominal 150 less a side assembly of 20 each side, which is an estimate.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on each face is the channel between the two side assemblies, 110 wide, run down the height (`run: y`). Its finger pitch is the rack unit, 44.45; the gap between arms is the pitch less the arm's estimated 12.

left.note: estimated - the side, rear at x=0: 48 arms and heads at one rack unit on each face and a door at each end. The side is open between the arms and across the centre, as the data sheet's photographs show a side of slots.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET'S ORDERING MATRIX; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM ITS TEXT AND THE INSTALLATION DRAWINGS. The Motive Cable Management data sheet (MKT-60020-675, 09/24) (page 3) builds the part number 32620-703 from a style (2, double-sided, black fingers), a width (6 in, 150 mm), a colour (Black) and a height (7 ft), and prints one overall depth for a double-sided manager, 23.6 in (600 mm). THE WIDTH AND THE HEIGHT ARE NOMINAL: the matrix prints them as sizes to order by, not as overall dimensions, and the figures here are taken as the overall size. The page 1 specifications and the installation instructions (IIS-737610) say what the manager is made of and how it is mounted and fitted with its doors. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: a guide, a side assembly, the track, the centre section and the door are estimated, each in its own entry below. Nothing was copied from a picture; the figures are transcribed.

mount.note: drawing - rack-side. The installation instructions (page 2) have the manager positioned next to the rack and attached with 4 M8 carriage bolts, washers and flange nuts at the upper and lower pairs of holes, and draw the double-sided manager with the mounting holes of a 3 in and a 6 in wide rack in its centre section, so it stands beside the rack, outside the rails, a face to the front and a face to the rear. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 48` is the 7 ft height over one rack unit and is estimated, because no held page says which racks a Motive height is for. The page 2 text says the manager is biased towards the rear on a 3 in wide rack; the model is drawn equal about its centre.

rear.note: estimated - the rear channel with its door fitted. The data sheet (page 1) lists a dual-hinged front door and rear door assembly, and the installation instructions (page 3) say the rear door is a plain flat door. No page draws the rear guides; the installation instructions' page 2 figure draws guides on both sides of the centre section and the rear is taken to be the front again, 48 a side.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides.

shell.note: drawing - a hollow manager, as every manager in the library is. The body is a sheet body and its views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: a frame and the guides on each face, and the two doors that lift off.

spine.note: estimated - the centre section, 198 deep between the two channels, with the central track and the mounting holes for the rack (installation instructions, page 2). The page 2 figure draws the rear guides, the centre and the front guides about equal in depth, so each is a third of the overall depth less the doors. The figure is not to a stated scale. The data sheet (page 6) sells a Mid Panel Kit that 'covers and divides the front and rear', so none is fitted: the centre is open in the side views.

thickness.note: estimated - no held page states a wall gauge. 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in the library; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: estimated - the end of the manager seen from above, rear at y=0: a door 3 thick at each end, a channel of 198 at each, and the centre section of 198 between. The 600 is the data sheet's; the split is the estimate of the centre section, the guide and the frame.
